anti_overlap: Do not evaluate the technical correctness of the microrouter design findings — fd-architecture and fd-safety cover those
Do not assess workstream sequencing for schedule purposes — fd-broadcast-scheduling covers slot ordering
Do not evaluate test coverage gaps — fd-kaizen-testability covers those
decision_lens: A handoff that omits a known risk is not a neutral omission — it is an active transfer of that risk to the incoming agent operating without warning. Evaluate the roadmap's handoff artifacts (beads, design docs, handoff markdown files) for completeness: does the incoming session have everything it needs to avoid re-discovering known dead ends, or does it have to reconstruct context that was already earned?
distance_rationale: Hospital charge nurses manage shift-handoff completeness as a patient-safety discipline, where omitted context directly causes adverse events — structurally identical to multi-session agent work where incomplete bead bodies or Dolt drift cause downstream sessions to operate on a false-clean state, but in a clinical care context rather than software.
expected_isomorphisms: Shift handoff record omitting a known risk maps to a bead body that names a finding without describing the failure scenario. 'Mental model never externalized' maps to Architecture α/β decision criteria existing only in a handoff file, not in the bead. False-clean state on incoming shift maps to Dolt missing 14 P0 beads.
focus: Knowledge transfer completeness, session-to-session continuity gaps, and compounding failure modes in multi-session multi-agent handoff chains
name: fd-handoff-fidelity
persona: Apply the perspective of a hospital charge nurse managing shift handoff rotations in a complex care unit — one who knows that most preventable adverse events trace to incomplete handoffs: information that existed in one shift's mental model but was never externalized into the transfer record, leaving the incoming team to rediscover known risks from scratch.
review_areas: Assess the bead/JSONL drift (14 microrouter finding beads + s3z6.19.x only in issues.jsonl, not in live Dolt) as a handoff gap: an incoming session that queries Dolt directly will not see these beads, creating a risk of duplicate work or contradictory decisions

Check the handoff coverage of the four P0 Track B6 findings (jm4/emv/a5u/906): does each finding bead contain enough context for a cold-start session to understand the failure scenario without reading the full flux-review transcript? Flag findings that are named but not described

Verify that the Architecture α/β fork decision — described as 'the deepest finding' in the handoff — has its decision criteria and current state externalized in a durable artifact, not only in session memory or prose notes

Assess the interflect scaffold status (recent commits 8e027b22, d3f47fc9): a 'scaffold' companion plugin that feeds retrospective compounding is only useful if its output format and integration path are documented before it accumulates session data that cannot be retrospectively compounded

Check whether the 'bead/code drift' warning (sylveste-n6zw open while commit reports 17/18 shipped) has a stated verification procedure — an unresolved drift without a check procedure will recur; flag if no procedure is defined

Evaluate the research-mode parity gap (peer findings, reaction round, sycophancy detection missing from research mode): does the roadmap capture what a research-mode session is missing in a way that would prevent it from silently producing incomplete output, or is the gap only visible to someone who has read the full roadmap?

severity_examples.condition: When the push.sh step to sync JSONL→Dolt has not been run and no session guard prevents Dolt-only queries from returning a false-clean state
severity_examples.scenario: The live Dolt DB is missing all 14 microrouter finding beads — an incoming session querying Dolt for open P0 items will see zero Track B6 P0s, and may proceed as if the safety-floor bypass and circular calibration issues are resolved

severity_examples.condition: When the bead body for s3z6.19.8 does not include the α/β fork definition and the criteria for choosing between them
severity_examples.scenario: Architecture α/β decision criteria exist only in a handoff document, not in the s3z6.19.8 bead body — a new session working on .19.8 must re-read the handoff file or risk re-opening a settled design question

severity_examples.condition: When interflect commits show scaffold-only state with no schema or integration spec committed alongside
severity_examples.scenario: interflect's retrospective compounding format is not documented before it begins accumulating session data — sessions that produce interflect output cannot be retrospectively compounded into its intended knowledge format if the schema is defined after the data

success_hints: For each P0 finding bead, check: can a session that has never read the flux-review transcript understand the failure scenario from the bead body alone? If not, flag the gap with the specific missing context

Distinguish between 'context in a handoff file' (session-scoped, may be pruned) and 'context in a bead body' (durable, queryable) — findings that exist only in handoff files are at risk of being lost across session boundaries
When assessing drift (bead/code, Dolt/JSONL), check both directions: code ahead of bead AND bead ahead of code — the roadmap audit flags the former but the latter is also a failure mode
task_context: The interflux v0.2.68 roadmap has multiple handoff artifacts: bead files, JSONL exports, design docs, and handoff markdown. The bead audit section flags Dolt/JSONL drift and an open-but-shipped bead state. Review through the lens of shift handoff fidelity: does each durable artifact contain enough context for an incoming session to operate safely, or is critical context trapped in session memory or ephemeral prose?
